conversations.seed: I spent my whole life being the 'good, smart kid' to make my family happy. Now that I'm on my own, I have no idea what I actually like.

conversations.content: I spent my whole life being the 'good, smart kid' to make my family happy. Now that I'm on my own, I have no idea what I actually like.
What does it feel like to be 'the good, smart kid' all the time?
I don't know, it just feels suffocating. Like I'm living someone else's dream, not mine.
You feel like you're living someone else's dream. Is that scary to admit?
Yes, it's terrifying. Because what if that's all I'm capable of? What if I'm just not good enough?
You're worried that you're not good enough. What does that feel like in your body?
It feels like a weight is crushing me. I just want to be done with it all.
You feel like you want to be done with it all. Have you ever felt like that before, even when things were going well?
No, never. But now I'm starting to feel like I don't even know who I am.
You're starting to feel like you don't even know who you are. What does that feel like, exactly?
You've been carrying the pressure to be 'the good, smart kid' for so long. What does it feel like to even consider letting that go?
That makes sense. What would feel like one small step — not a plan, just one thing — to start letting go of that expectation?
